fixes.explanation: Whoa, careful, friend, that one flips it! Paul says the opposite: “Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.” (Galatians 5:8). Think about what that tells us. The One who calls them is the One who got them running in the first place. So the voice slowing them down is a different voice, and it's not His. I once followed a voice that said 'this drawer is home now,' and let me tell you, that voice was not the One who called me out.

False, and Paul wastes no time. “Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.” (Galatians 5:8). Notice he asks who obstructed them, but he doesn't hand over a name. He just rules out one source. The One who called them isn't the One tugging them off course. Good catch, baker!

Whoa, flip that one over, friend. Paul says the opposite: “The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.” (Galatians 5:10). Nobody walks away from troubling the Galatians with a free pass. Paul says it right after he states his confidence in the Lord, and I think he wants them to know the One they trust is not asleep on this. This is a heavy line, so I'll leave it right there.

problems.problem: The lane and swerving imagery restates Paul's running picture, while checking the source adds little insight or personality.
The explanation still mostly restates that the persuasion did not come from the One who calls them; asking where it came from adds little insight.
Calling Paul steady rather than shaky restates his confidence, and calling the line heavy adds little insight or personality.
